- For an individual investor, the practical Claude stack is: equity-research + financial-analysis plugins (skills work without paid connectors if you supply filings) + one cheap data MCP (Financial Datasets/Alpha Vantage/Yahoo for US; Kite MCP/Trendlyne for India) + saved red-team prompts.
- Institutional connectors (FactSet, S&P, Morningstar) are the main moat of "Claude for Financial Services"; retail users will mostly lack them.

`case_study:paytm-ipo-2021` | 2021-11-18 | tickers: PAYTM | confidence: verified

One 97 Communications (Paytm) raised Rs 18,300 cr at Rs 2,150/share in Nov 2021 (then India's largest IPO; ~Rs 10,000 cr was offer-for-sale by existing holders). It listed at Rs 1,950 on 18 Nov 2021 and closed at Rs 1,564 (-27%), the worst mainboard debut by size. By Nov 2022 it was ~79% below issue (~Rs 440s). In Mar 2022 RBI barred Paytm Payments Bank (an associate) from onboarding customers; on 31 Jan 2024 RBI ordered PPBL to stop most deposit/credit business from Feb-Mar 2024 citing 'persistent non-compliances', and the stock hit back-to-back 20% lower circuits to ~Rs 300-440 range (exact low unverified). It later recovered substantially as losses narrowed (2024-25). Visible flags at IPO: (1) loss-making since inception with no clear path to profit; (2) valuation ~50x sales-ish on a payments business with near-zero UPI margins; (3) big OFS = insiders selling; (4) QIB book subscribed only ~2.8x; (5) Macquarie's pre-listing Rs 1,200 target (-44%); (6) regulatory dependence on a related payments bank. Lesson: IPOs where insiders sell most of the issue at peak private valuations have poor base rates; regulator actions on a related entity are a key risk. Not a fraud -- a valuation and regulatory blowup, partly reversed.

**Lesson:** Avoid IPOs priced at last private round with heavy OFS; check regulatory dependence
**Spotted early by:** Macquarie (Suresh Ganapathy)
